name: Artemis Medicare Services Ltd
tagline: Apollo Tyres-promoter hospital operator with a real Q1 FY27 operating-leverage inflection (PAT +48%, occupancy 65.7%) and an asset-light bed-expansion plan - but at ~Rs 5,100 Cr and hospital-rollout speed, the return math does not fit the 10x/100x thesis
business_overview: Artemis runs multi-specialty hospitals under the Artemis Hospitals brand, anchored by its ~600-bed flagship in Gurugram (Haryana) and expanding into new geographies (200-bed Artemis Shanti Hospital, Raipur, opened July 2026; +200-bed pediatric/gynae block approved at Gurugram). Promoted by the Apollo Tyres (Onkar Kanwar) group; the underlying hospital property is leased from group entity PTL Enterprises. The bull thesis flagged by SEBI RIA @suru27 on X is that Artemis can scale toward ~2,000 beds largely asset-light - via 30-year hospital operating/management contracts plus purchased FAR (floor-area ratio) - sidestepping the land scarcity and capex drag that slows metro hospital rollouts.
fundamentals_table: FY25 +8.1% (5-yr CAGR ~10%); Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 287 Cr +12.7% YoY
EBITDA Rs 62 Cr +27.9%; PAT Rs 31.4 Cr +48.3%; bed occupancy 65.7% vs 61.2% YoY
~75% over 5 yrs (off a low, maturing-asset base)
fundamentals_narrative: Trailing figures are unremarkable for a hospital chain - ~8-10% revenue growth, ~12% ROE - but Q1 FY27 shows a genuine operating-leverage turn: revenue +12.7%, EBITDA +27.9%, PAT +48.3%, and occupancy up ~450 bps to 65.7% as the flagship matures and new blocks fill. Balance sheet is comfortable (D/E 0.26). The forward driver is bed addition (Raipur live; Gurugram pediatric/gynae block approved; medium-term ambition ~2,000 beds via asset-light operating pacts + purchased FAR). This is a credible multi-year compounder, but bed rollout is inherently slow and the stock already trades at a full valuation for a regional operator.

bull_case: Q1 FY27 confirms an operating-leverage inflection: PAT +48%, EBITDA margin ~21.5% (+270 bps), occupancy 65.7% vs 61.2% - the maturing-asset thesis is showing in the numbers
Asset-light expansion path (30-yr operating/management contracts + purchased FAR) could roughly triple bed capacity toward ~2,000 without a proportionate capex/land drag
Comfortable balance sheet (D/E 0.26) and a credible promoter group (Apollo Tyres / Kanwar family)
New-geography entry (Raipur) diversifies away from single-hospital (Gurugram) concentration
5-yr PAT CAGR ~75% off a low base - if occupancy and new blocks keep filling, earnings can compound well above revenue
bear_case: At ~Rs 5,124 Cr a literal 10x in 2-3 years needs ~Rs 51,000 Cr - not achievable for a regional hospital operator adding beds on a multi-year schedule; 100x in 10 years is not realistic either
Trailing fundamentals are modest: ROE ~12%, revenue growth ~8-10% - the quality gate is only borderline cleared
Still heavily dependent on the single Gurugram flagship; new units (Raipur) take years to reach mature occupancy/margins
Property leased from promoter group entity (PTL Enterprises) - related-party rent is a structural leakage to watch
Full valuation already: the known operating-leverage story is at least partly in the price near the top of the 52-week range
The ~2,000-bed / purchased-FAR plan is management ambition, not yet contracted, funded, and executing at scale
verdict_headline: Genuine Q1 FY27 operating-leverage turn and a sensible asset-light growth plan, but hospital-rollout economics can't deliver a 2-3yr 10x or a 10yr 100x from Rs 5,100 Cr
verdict_reasoning: Recent-quarter inflection is real and specific (PAT +48%, occupancy +450 bps), so this is not a case of a trailing average hiding a turn - the turn is visible; the constraint is magnitude, not direction
Bed capacity is going from ~600 toward maybe ~1,200-1,400 over ~3 years even on the bullish plan - that is a ~3-5x earnings path over 4-5 years, a good compounder but well short of 10x-in-2-3-years

Mid-cap size with no named management/regulatory regime change (the asset-light model is a capital-allocation choice, not a structural inflection of the large-cap-exception type), and a full valuation, keep thesis_fit at 'neither'
